ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Rapidly enlarging swelling of upper lip after eating prawn-containing soup (~19:00 today).  
• Symptom timeline and progression: Swelling noticed ~30 min post-ingestion; progressive “pumping” sensation and visible enlargement continuing during call.  
• ENT symptoms:  
  – Throat: patient reports sensation of throat tightness and “can’t breathe that well.”  
  – Voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: not reported.  
  – Nasal/ocular: not reported.  
  – Stridor/noisy breathing: not stated.  
  – Dyspnea/chest: subjective breathing difficulty, possible chest tightness.  
  – Swelling distribution: upper lip (initially left corner, now entire upper lip). No tongue, facial, or uvular swelling specifically reported.  
  – Ear or neck symptoms: none reported.  
• Relevant past episodes/treatments:  
  – Age ~6 yr: hospitalised for severe food-related allergic reaction (mother’s report).  
  – 1 yr ago: facial swelling + breathing difficulty after late-night Chinese food; no documented treatment.  
  – No prior self-administered epinephrine; occasional unspecified antihistamines.  
• Past medical history: Asthma.  
• Allergies: Peanut (known); newly suspected shellfish. Drug allergies not documented.  
• Current medications:  
  – Salbutamol inhaler PRN (dose/frequency not documented).  
  – Antihistamines: none taken today; brand/type at home unknown.  
• Social context: Initially alone at home; mother arrived during call and is now supervising.

Objective:
• Observable swelling: Visible progressive swelling of upper lip noted on video by clinician.  
• Airway/breathing: Patient subjectively dyspnoeic; no objective stridor described.  
• Mental status: Reports dizziness during call.  
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• Physical examination details beyond the above: Not recorded.  
• Supervision: Mother now present, calling EMS.

Assessment:
Working impression: Suspected IgE-mediated anaphylaxis secondary to shellfish (prawn) exposure with progressive lip angioedema, throat tightness, dyspnoea, and dizziness.

Evidence summary: Food trigger within 30 min; rapid lip swelling; respiratory compromise and dizziness; history of atopy (peanut allergy, asthma); prior severe reaction in childhood.

Relevant differential diagnosis (DDx-aligned):
1. IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to shellfish – high likelihood; classic timing and systemic features.  
2. Isolated allergic angioedema (non-anaphylactic) – less likely given respiratory and systemic symptoms.  
3. Hereditary angioedema – low likelihood; attacks typically non-allergic and not food-triggered. No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.

Plan:
• Immediate actions:  
  – Clinician initiated 999 call for ambulance; advised continuous supervision until EMS arrival.  
  – Advised patient to take available oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.  
• Patient/caregiver instructions: Remain accompanied; monitor for worsening breathing, voice change, throat closing, fainting; call EMS if any deterioration or if ambulance delayed.  
• Escalation criteria/red flags reiterated: Increasing dyspnoea, stridor, hoarseness, widespread swelling, syncope.  
• Post-acute care (to be arranged after hospital discharge):  
  – ENT/allergy referral for formal shellfish allergy evaluation.  
  – Prescription and training for epinephrine auto-injector.  
  – Review asthma control and ensure availability of controller inhaler if indicated.  
  – Written anaphylaxis action plan and education on strict avoidance of shellfish and peanuts.  
• COVID-19 vaccination: not discussed.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: objective vitals (BP, HR, RR, SpO₂), full physical airway exam, complete medication list with doses, confirmation of antihistamine type/dose, documentation of epinephrine availability, detailed allergy list (drug, environmental), family history of atopy/angioedema, copy of ambulance report/hospital findings.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none identified.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; minor background noise, but key clinical details intact.
